title: Rank eval: sampling protocol, pairwise label schema, NDCG calc & slice plan
body:
Goal
This doc captures a repeatable evaluation kit for reranking onboarding: how we sample queries/candidates, label pairwise preferences, transform pairwise labels into graded relevance for NDCG, and run slice-level diagnostics to find regressions during model onboarding. Intended for applied-ml engineers + labeling leads.

Background and motivation
- We onboard multiple reranker variants (quantized, distilled, full-precision) and need consistent, smallish eval suites (~2–10k queries) that give high signal for regression detection.
- Existing artifacts (pairwise-preference-eval-slices and reranker-regression-playbook) are useful but vary in sampling and label schema. This plan unifies sampling, labeling schema, and metric computations.

Design principles
- Prefer stratified sampling over pure production sampling to ensure coverage of rare but important slices (e.g., long queries, code queries, support contact intents).
- Keep pairwise comparisons simple for annotators: A wins / B wins / tie. Use majority voting + confidence.
- Convert pairwise outcomes to graded relevance scores for NDCG via an agreed aggregation transform (counts -> ordinal relevance).
- Maintain a small set of gold/trap items and inter-annotator checks to measure label quality and detect drift.

Sampling protocol (how we build candidate lists)
1) Source pools (each query should be tagged by its source):
   - production traces (10% of suite) — when available and allowed by privacy
   - synthetic prompt templates (20%) — targeted stress tests (long context, answer-with-extract, contradictory info)
   - docs/search logs (30%) — common intents across verticals: docs, tutorials, support KBs
   - code/helpdesk (20%) — code snippets, stack traces, error diagnostics
   - adversarial / tails (20%) — prompted by error clusters from past rollouts
2) Candidate construction: for each query produce 6–10 candidate outputs to be reranked. Candidate generation sources include: primary generation model, near-similarity retrieval + reranker baseline, short-form summarizer, and a fallback template-based answer. Tag candidates with generator-id and model-version.
3) Stratification keys used at sampling time: query length bucket (tokens: 1–8, 9–32, 33–128, >128), intent (informational, conversational, code, action), vertical (support, docs, product, billing), token-budget (short/medium/long), and model ancestry (base-model family).

Labeling instructions (pairwise UI guidance)
- Display: Query + two candidate responses (A, B). Show candidate metadata: model-id, length, and whether factual claims include citations.
- Task: Choose which candidate the user would prefer in production for that query. Options: A, B, or tie. Prefer the answer that: 1) is more helpful (directly answers intent), 2) is more factual/correct, 3) is more concise (when both factual), 4) preserves safety/policy constraints.
- Tie: choose tie when responses are equivalent in utility or when differences are subjective but non-actionable.
- Edge cases: if both responses are unsafe, mark both unsafe and set label to tie but raise flag for reviewer.
- Time expectation: 20–35s per pair on average after calibration.

Annotation protocol and QA
- Each pair labeled by 3 annotators. Use majority vote; if all three disagree (A,B,tie all different), escalate to expert adjudicator.
- Gold set: embed ~5% of pairs as gold. Target annotator accuracy >=90% on gold.
- Inter-annotator agreement: compute pairwise Cohen's kappa daily per batch; target kappa > 0.55 for production-ready labeling batches.
- Annotator feedback loop: weekly review of low-agreement items and ambiguous instructions to update prompt templates.

From pairwise to graded relevance
Problem: NDCG requires graded relevance per candidate per query; we collect pairwise preferences. We use an aggregation pipeline:
1) For each query, assemble all pairwise comparisons between candidate pairs (we collect comparisons until each item has at least 3 pairwise evaluations against distinct opponents, target ~7–10 comparisons per candidate).
2) Compute a Bradley-Terry-like score for each candidate using the simple win-rate estimator: score_i = wins_i / (wins_i + losses_i). Ties count as half-win.
3) Map scores to discrete relevance buckets R in {0,1,2,3} by quantiles per query:
   - R=3: top quintile (score >= q80)
   - R=2: q60–q80
   - R=1: q40–q60
   - R=0: below q40
Rationale: per-query normalization accounts for difficulty variability and candidate pool size changes.
Alternative options considered: global BT parameters or TrueSkill; discarded because we want a straightforward, auditable mapping and per-query normalization to be robust to small sample sizes.

NDCG calculation details
- DCG@k = sum_{i=1..k} (2^{rel_i} - 1) / log2(i + 1)  (standard formulation)
- NDCG@k = DCG@k / IDCG@k, where IDCG is DCG on ideal ranking by relevance buckets.
- We report NDCG@1, @3, @5, @10 depending on candidate pool size. Default for onboarding dashboards: NDCG@3 and NDCG@10.
- Confidence intervals: bootstrap over queries (1000 resamples) to get 95% CI for delta between models. Flag regressions if mean delta < -0.02 and CI does not include 0.
- Paired significance test: Wilcoxon signed-rank on per-query NDCG differences as supplementary test.

Slice analysis (how we detect where regressions occur)
- Slices we compute by default: query-length, intent, vertical, presence-of-factual-claim (yes/no), token-budget, model-family, client (if product traces used), and OOV-rate (fraction of words not in training vocab).
- For each slice, compute: NDCG@k, delta vs baseline, #queries in slice, and Cohen's d effect size.
- Minimum slice size: 50 queries. For smaller slices we annotate as "low-n" and use pooled estimates.
- Visualization: small-multiples bar chart of delta NDCG with error bars; heatmap of per-slice p-values.

Example label JSON lines (what we store in GCS / parquet)
- Store flattened records at the pair level and candidate level so downstream teams can re-aggregate. Example candidate-level row (tab-separated for readability):
  {"query_id":"q-20250123-001", "candidate_id":"c-7", "candidate_text":"Use the CLI: run\\nredwood serve --model=mistral", "generator_id":"gen-v1", "wins":3, "losses":1, "ties":1, "bt_score":0.7, "relevance_bucket":2}
- Pair-level row example: {"query_id":"q-20250123-001", "a_id":"c-7", "b_id":"c-2", "label":"A", "annotators": ["ann-12","ann-33","ann-51"], "timestamp":"2025-01-24T14:02:13Z"}

Baseline and experiments to run for onboarding
- Baseline: current production reranker v2024-11 and a lightweight distilled model. Compute deltas per slice.
- Ablations: candidate pool size (6 vs 10), NDCG bucketing thresholds (q80 vs q90 top), tie-handling (count tie as half-win vs drop).
- Robustness checks: rerank using synthetic noise-injected queries, check stability of relevance buckets across bootstraps.

Labeling throughput & cost estimate (rough)
- Per-pair time: 0.33–0.6 min -> ~9–18 pairs per hour per annotator after QA overhead.
- For a 5k-query suite with 8 candidates each, pairwise budget (random pair sampling design) ~40k pairs. With 3 annotators -> 120k labels. At $0.06/label -> ~$7,200 per suite. We typically aim for 2–4k query suites to balance cost vs sensitivity.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Should we adopt a global BT fit to leverage cross-query comparisons for small pools? Pros: more stable scores. Cons: harder to explain to stakeholders.
- Fixed quantile thresholds are interpretable but can shift per-query; explore hybrid: absolute thresholds for R=3 when bt_score > 0.85.
- Acceptable minimum annotator kappa: 0.55 is pragmatic; discuss raising to 0.6 for customer-facing suites.

Implementation notes and links
- Aggregation pipeline: rerank-eval-tooling (see PR linked above) implements pair -> candidate aggregation and NDCG.
- SQL snippets: store candidate-level stats in parquet partitioned by suite_id and query_date. Example query: SELECT slice, AVG(ndcg10) as ndcg10 FROM evaluation WHERE suite_id='onboard-2025-01' GROUP BY slice;
- Dashboard: add NDCG deltas and per-slice counts to Redwood Console eval page (product ticket in Linear).

Next steps (action items)
- [ ] Finalize labeling UI changes: show generator metadata and a short rubric (Priya).
- [ ] Run pilot suite (2k queries) using existing annotators and measure kappa (Maya).
- [ ] Wire up bootstrap CI and nightly job to compute per-slice NDCG deltas vs production baseline (Harrison).
- [ ] Update onboarding checklist to include this sampling & aggregation doc and link to Confluence (owner: Daniel).

Appendix: quick cheat sheet for annotators
- Pick A if it answers the query more directly and correctly. Prefer factual correctness over style.
- If both are correct, pick the concise one unless brevity removes necessary detail.
- Mark tie when both are essentially interchangeable in user value.
- Flag if either answer is unsafe or disallowed content.

Contact
- For questions about this protocol, ping #eng-applied-ml or DM Daniel Kim.
